newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's ousted Lebed blasts his successor Rybkin.
newsitem.headline: Russia's ousted Lebed blasts his successor Rybkin.

text.p: Outspoken general Alexander Lebed, ousted as Russian security chief earlier this week, blasted his successor Ivan Rybkin on Saturday as an incompetent bureaucrat, Interfax news agency said.
The agency quoted Lebed as saying Rybkin was "unable to ensure the security of the country at a time when there are many dangers facing it".
Under Rybkin, the Security Council would "turn into a quiet bureaucratic office that no one will know about".
President Boris Yeltsin named Rybkin on Saturday as successor to Lebed's two posts -- secretary of the powerful Security Council and envoy to rebel Chechnya.
Yeltsin dramatically sacked Lebed on Thursday as his security supremo, accusing him in a televised speech of lack of team spirit and naked presidential ambitions.
Rybkin was speaker of the State Duma lower house of parliament from 1994 to 1995. He is a moderate who firmly steered the Duma away from any clashes with the president.
"He (Rybkin) will behave like he did in his time at the Duma when he would calmly continue speaking from his presiding chair while deputies were fighting in the hall," Lebed said.
